concepts.label: test-driven development
concepts.definition: Developing by first writing an automated test that fails, then making it pass, then refactoring the code while keeping behavior working.

concepts.label: refactoring
concepts.definition: Changing software's internal structure to make it easier to understand or cheaper to modify without changing its observable behavior.

concepts.label: design by contract
concepts.definition: Specifying explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and state invariants as responsibilities between software elements.

references.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
references.locator: Pragmatic Paranoia, Topic 23, Design by Contract and Implementing DBC

concepts.label: mutation testing
concepts.definition: Assessing tests by deliberately changing production code and checking whether the tests detect those changes.

concepts.label: ubiquitous language
concepts.definition: A shared, precise domain-model language used by developers and domain experts.

concepts.label: property-based testing
concepts.definition: Testing general properties over generated input domains and seeking counterexamples when a property fails.

concepts.label: accidental complexity
concepts.definition: Complexity introduced by the chosen implementation rather than inherent in the problem being solved.

references.title: The Mythical Man-Month
references.locator: Chapter 16, No Silver Bullet; Essence and Accidents

concepts.label: dead code
concepts.definition: Code or configuration that is no longer used and can be removed without losing needed behavior.

references.title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code

concepts.label: smoke test
concepts.definition: A small set of checks establishing that a build or deployment runs and its main functions and dependencies are available.

references.title: Continuous Delivery
references.locator: Deployment Pipeline Practices, Smoke-Test Your Deployments

concepts.label: separation of duties
concepts.definition: Assigning distinct responsibilities to different actors, including a maker and an independent checker, so one actor does not perform and approve all work.

references.title: NIST CSRC Glossary: Separation of Duty

concepts.label: deep module
concepts.definition: A module that provides substantial useful functionality through an interface requiring comparatively little knowledge to use.
concepts.scopeNote: Depth relates functionality to interface complexity, not implementation size. Interface leverage is a practitioner elaboration, not a universal workflow.

concepts.label: information hiding
concepts.definition: Organizing modules around design decisions they conceal, especially decisions likely to change, and exposing only what other modules need.
concepts.scopeNote: Private fields alone do not hide a decision if clients depend on its representation. This is not confidentiality.

references.title: David Parnas: On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules

concepts.label: make illegal states unrepresentable
concepts.definition: Choosing types or data representations that exclude invalid combinations rather than merely checking for them after construction.
concepts.scopeNote: Guarantees depend on constructors, language features and escape hatches; runtime checks on an otherwise permissive representation are not the same property.

references.title: Scott Wlaschin: Making illegal states unrepresentable

concepts.label: parse, don't validate
concepts.definition: Converting less-structured input into a stronger representation that preserves established facts, instead of checking and discarding those facts.
concepts.scopeNote: Parsing includes validation; a Boolean check followed by an unchecked cast does not preserve the guarantee in the same way.

concepts.label: branded types
concepts.definition: Distinguishing values with the same underlying representation but different semantic roles so typed code cannot freely interchange them.
concepts.scopeNote: Branding alone does not validate external input or provide runtime security isolation. Nominal types, opaque types and newtypes are related, not unrestricted synonyms.

concepts.label: functional core, imperative shell
concepts.definition: Placing decisions and transformations in pure functions, with I/O and other side effects in an outer coordination layer.
concepts.scopeNote: Folder separation alone is insufficient; hidden global reads and I/O remain effects. The talk page establishes provenance; the practitioner source supplies operational detail.

concepts.label: design it twice
concepts.definition: Exploring substantially different designs and their trade-offs before committing to one.
concepts.scopeNote: A named principle attributed to Ousterhout in Pocock's guidance, not a requirement for subagents. Two reviewers or two execution attempts do not establish alternative designs.

concepts.label: characterization testing
concepts.definition: Writing tests to document what existing software actually does rather than what it ought to do.
concepts.scopeNote: Recorded behavior is not certified correct. Characterization tests may later serve as regression tests; snapshots are only one technique.

concepts.label: differential testing
concepts.definition: Giving the same inputs to implementations or versions expected to agree and investigating differences in their results.
concepts.scopeNote: A disagreement alone does not identify the faulty implementation; intentionally different specifications are not a suitable agreement oracle.

references.title: Csmith: Finding and Reporting Bugs in C Compilers

concepts.label: change-detector test
concepts.definition: A test that reproduces implementation information and reacts to implementation changes without independently checking required behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: Mocks, snapshots and interaction assertions are not automatically change detectors: an interaction can itself be required behavior. Tautological testing is related, not an exact alias.

references.title: Alex Eagle: Change-Detector Tests Considered Harmful

concepts.label: test isolation
concepts.definition: Keeping tests independent so one test's state or effects do not determine another test's outcome.
concepts.scopeNote: Serial execution is not isolation. Collaborator isolation is a different usage; isolated browser contexts do not isolate a shared database.

concepts.label: hermetic testing
concepts.definition: Running tests in a self-contained, controlled environment without assumptions about uncontrolled outside state or resources.
concepts.scopeNote: A container or one mocked request is insufficient. Hermetic tests can span multiple processes and need not be unit tests.

concepts.label: idempotency
concepts.definition: The property that repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once.
concepts.scopeNote: Responses and logs may differ. This does not promise exactly-once execution; request deduplication is a possible mechanism.

concepts.label: blast radius
concepts.definition: The scope of effects or disruption that a change or failure can have, including indirect consumers and operational behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: Change-impact analysis investigates this scope; the activity and the scope are not unrestricted synonyms. A caller list is not proof of impact or safety, nor permission to expand a change.

concepts.label: ablation study
concepts.definition: Assessing a component's contribution by removing it and comparing system performance under otherwise comparable conditions.
concepts.scopeNote: Changing several factors does not isolate one contribution. No statistical significance, retraining or broad generalization is implied.

concepts.label: progressive disclosure
concepts.definition: Presenting essential information or options first and revealing secondary detail when needed.
concepts.scopeNote: Hiding essential prerequisites is not successful disclosure. Mandatory sequential steps are staged disclosure, not necessarily progressive disclosure; context-loading applications imply no measured token savings.

concepts.label: DRY
concepts.definition: Giving each piece of system knowledge one authoritative representation instead of maintaining parallel representations independently.
concepts.scopeNote: Similar-looking code can express different knowledge; textual duplication alone does not establish duplicated knowledge.

references.title: Hunt and Thomas: DRY excerpt
references.locator: DRY is More Than Code; Not All Code Duplication is Knowledge Duplication

concepts.label: YAGNI
concepts.definition: Not implementing a capability now solely because it is anticipated to be needed in the future.
concepts.scopeNote: Not a reason to neglect current testing, refactoring or design health. Avoiding speculative capabilities differs from removing unused code or unnecessary implementation complexity.

concepts.label: orthogonality
concepts.definition: Independence of aspects of a system that allows them to vary without requiring unrelated changes elsewhere.
concepts.scopeNote: Separate files alone do not establish independence. Orthogonality concerns independent variation, not merely fewer dependencies.

references.title: Hunt and Thomas: Orthogonality and the DRY Principle

concepts.label: high cohesion
concepts.definition: Grouping a coherent set of responsibilities or concepts that belong together within a module.
concepts.scopeNote: Small size or one public method alone does not establish cohesion. Cohesion concerns what belongs together, not the number of dependencies.

concepts.label: low coupling
concepts.definition: Limiting dependencies so modules can be understood and changed with relatively little knowledge of each other.
concepts.scopeNote: Zero dependencies is not the goal; splitting files can increase relationships.

concepts.label: value object
concepts.definition: A domain concept distinguished by its values rather than conceptual identity, usually with immutable behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: An immutable entity with persistent identity remains an entity; a DTO is not automatically a value object.

concepts.label: regression testing
concepts.definition: Testing after changes for unintended damage to previously working behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: Testing only a new capability is insufficient. This is not synonymous with running every test or performing a smoke test.

concepts.label: contract testing
concepts.definition: Checking that an external-service double behaves consistently with the real service for interactions consumers rely on.
concepts.scopeNote: This glossary uses the narrow service-double meaning. Schema checks may establish only part of a contract; design by contract and consumer-driven contract testing are not unrestricted aliases.

concepts.label: fuzzing
concepts.definition: Automatically exercising software with generated or mutated inputs to seek failures.
concepts.scopeNote: Mutating inputs is not production-code mutation testing. Random load without failure checks is insufficient.

concepts.label: debugging by bisection
concepts.definition: Repeatedly testing intermediate revisions between known contrasting endpoints to locate a behavior-changing revision.
concepts.scopeNote: Sequential commit testing or history reading is not bisection. Flaky or non-monotonic outcomes can mislead; git bisect is a tool, not the universal concept name.

concepts.label: optimistic concurrency control
concepts.definition: Allowing concurrent work, then validating relevant shared state before committing and rejecting or retrying conflicts.
concepts.scopeNote: Suppressing an obsolete UI response is not validating a shared-state write. Optimistic Offline Lock is a specific pattern, not an unrestricted alias.

concepts.label: expand-contract migration
concepts.definition: Expanding an interface or schema compatibly, migrating consumers, then removing the old form.
concepts.scopeNote: A one-shot rename or gradual rollout alone does not supply transitional compatibility. Independently deployed consumers can benefit; atomic internal migrations do not universally require it.

concepts.label: least privilege
concepts.definition: Giving users and processes only the privileges and resources necessary for their assigned function.
concepts.scopeNote: Limiting authority differs from assigning responsibilities to different actors, which is separation of duties.

concepts.label: Diátaxis
concepts.definition: Organizing documentation around tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanation according to the reader’s needs.
concepts.scopeNote: Not a synonym for concise prose or diagrams, nor a rule that all four forms belong in one document.

concepts.label: anticorruption layer
concepts.definition: A translation boundary between systems with different semantic models that keeps an external or legacy model from dictating the new domain's design.
concepts.scopeNote: A generic adapter or protocol conversion without significant semantic-model differences is insufficient. Bidirectional synchronization is an additional requirement, not implied. The Microsoft explanation attributes the pattern to Eric Evans.

concepts.label: metamorphic testing
concepts.definition: Testing expected relationships between results of related executions when checking individual outputs directly is difficult.
concepts.scopeNote: Related inputs must have an expected output relationship; multiple arbitrary runs are insufficient. Related to, not synonymous with, property-based testing.

references.title: Metamorphic testing and its applications to bioinformatics

concepts.label: delta debugging
concepts.definition: Automated reduction of failure-inducing material by testing smaller candidates while preserving the failure.
concepts.scopeNote: Asking for a small reproduction alone does not establish the reduction process. Global minimality is not promised.

concepts.label: bounded context
concepts.definition: An explicit scope within which a particular domain model applies consistently.
concepts.scopeNote: Not every service, repository or deployment boundary defines a bounded context. The same word can legitimately have different meanings across contexts.

concepts.label: separation of concerns
concepts.definition: Treating distinct aspects of a problem separately so each can be reasoned about without simultaneously considering all the others.
concepts.scopeNote: Does not require a particular folder structure or architecture. Distinct from assigning responsibilities to different actors (separation of duties).

references.title: Edsger Dijkstra: On the role of scientific thought

concepts.label: backpressure
concepts.definition: Regulating upstream production of work according to downstream capacity to receive or process it.
concepts.scopeNote: Bounded worker concurrency alone is insufficient if producers keep filling an unbounded queue. The upstream response to capacity is essential.

concepts.label: exponential backoff with jitter
concepts.definition: Retrying with delays that grow exponentially, commonly up to a cap, while randomizing timing to spread retries.
concepts.scopeNote: Does not imply safe retries, a deadline or a particular jitter distribution. A fixed delay, exponential delay alone or randomness alone is insufficient.

references.title: AWS Builders’ Library: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter

concepts.label: circuit breaker
concepts.definition: Temporarily stopping calls to a failing dependency after a failure threshold is reached, with a mechanism to test recovery before normal calls resume.
concepts.scopeNote: Distinct from retrying with longer delays or permanently disabling a feature; recovery probing need not use a particular implementation.

concepts.label: canary deployment
concepts.definition: Exposing a new release to a limited portion of production and evaluating that exposure to decide whether rollout should continue.
concepts.scopeNote: Not merely staging, a gradual rollout without evaluation, or a smoke test after full rollout. Limited exposure does not guarantee safety.

references.title: The Site Reliability Workbook: Canarying Releases

concepts.label: reconciliation loop
concepts.definition: Repeatedly comparing desired state with observed state and taking corrective action toward convergence.
concepts.scopeNote: Reporting drift without corrective action is insufficient. A loop does not guarantee instantaneous convergence or eliminate the need for safe repeated actions.

concepts.label: blinded evaluation
concepts.definition: Concealing relevant identities or conditions from evaluators to reduce identity-driven judgment bias.
concepts.scopeNote: A different-family judge or independent reviewer alone does not establish blinding. Blinding does not itself isolate a component contribution or remove every bias.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests an automated failing test first, implementation sufficient to pass it, then refactoring before the next case.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No failing-test-first, pass, then refactor cycle is requested. Tests after implementation, rerunning tests, or test additions alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is test-driven development.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests changes to software's internal code structure to improve readability, design or duplication while preserving observable behavior, including actual renaming of code elements. A distinct behavior-preserving restructuring or cleanup step also matches within a larger request that adds a feature or fixes behavior; removing code established to be unreachable or unused can be such a step.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No behavior-preserving internal code change is requested. Adding behavior, fixing user-visible behavior, or changing external contracts alone does not match, but does not exclude a distinct behavior-preserving internal restructuring step in the same request. Documentation-only naming conventions alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is refactoring.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and persistent state invariants or responsibilities between software elements.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and state invariants or responsibilities are requested. Ordinary input validation, schema compatibility, or an isolated assertion alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is design by contract.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests deliberate changes to production code to assess whether tests detect the changed behavior.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No deliberate production-code changes to assess test detection are requested. Implementation edits, changing test inputs, fuzzing, or coverage measurement alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is mutation testing.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests that developers and domain experts use a shared precise vocabulary for the domain model.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No shared precise domain-model vocabulary for developers and domain experts is requested. Naming conventions, technical abbreviations, or an unrelated glossary alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is ubiquitous language.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests testing general correctness properties over generated inputs from a domain.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No tests of general correctness properties over generated inputs are requested. Hand-picked examples only, random performance runs without correctness properties, or production-code mutation alone without generated-property tests do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is property-based testing.

recognition.matches: Asks to keep a real change simple, avoid or remove unnecessary moving parts, effort or indirection in how a current need is met, or to justify existing or proposed complexity (e.g. 'keep it simple', 'no complete redesign', 'far too much work for this', 'is this more complicated than necessary').
recognition.doesNotMatch: Hypothetical or illustrative examples; questioning whether the whole design or approach is wrong (a redesign question); dropping a capability that is not needed (YAGNI); deleting unused code (dead code); quality audits that merely list complexity among many criteria; performance tuning.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is accidental complexity.

recognition.matches: Asks to find or remove code, configuration, installed files, services or infrastructure definitions that are no longer used, including leftovers of software that was removed or replaced.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Cleaning up git branches, worktrees, PRs or build artefacts; asking why something exists (Chesterton's fence); avoiding a not-yet-built feature (YAGNI); silencing warnings.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is dead code.

recognition.matches: After a change is merged or deployed, asks to confirm it is live and that the system works or behaves as expected in the target environment (e.g. 'PR merged, make sure everything is live', 'confirm nothing broke after deploying').
recognition.doesNotMatch: A request to commit, push or deploy that only asks for the deploy itself to happen; watching CI checks or a PR until it merges; running the full test suite before merge.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is smoke test.

recognition.matches: Asks that work produced by one agent or person be checked or approved by a different agent or person, including a coordinator validating subagents' work, a fresh reviewer, or implement-review-fix loops.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Asking about or researching such workflows or their terminology; self-review; delegation with no separate check; running tests or linters only.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is separation of duties.

recognition.matches: Asks to hide substantial coordination or functionality behind an interface callers can use without understanding the internal machinery.
recognition.doesNotMatch: A large implementation, a thin forwarding wrapper, fewer files, or hiding a changing representation alone without interface simplification. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is deep module.

recognition.matches: Asks to conceal a specific change-prone design decision or representation behind module operations so clients no longer depend on it.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Private-field syntax, secret management, or a generic request to simplify an interface without identifying a decision or representation to conceal. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is information hiding.

recognition.matches: Asks to design a new representation or replace a permissive one with types, variants or constrained construction that exclude specified invalid combinations from construction.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Runtime checks on the same permissive representation, unchecked casts, generic better typing, or distinguishing two IDs without invalid state combinations. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is make illegal states unrepresentable.

recognition.matches: Asks to transform external or weakly structured input into a stronger domain representation once, preserving established invariants for downstream code.
recognition.doesNotMatch: A Boolean validator discarding its evidence, an unchecked cast, routine format parsing without a stronger invariant, or redesigning internal state variants alone. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is parse, don't validate.

recognition.matches: Asks to introduce a type-level distinction between values with the same underlying representation but different semantic roles to prevent accidental interchange.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Renaming variables, validating string syntax alone, runtime authorization, or general discriminated-state variants without semantic same-representation distinctions. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is branded types.

recognition.matches: Asks to separate pure decisions or transformations from I/O and side effects, keeping effects in an outer coordinator so the decision logic runs on values.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Merely separating controller and service files, mocking I/O without moving effects out of decision logic, or a purity claim despite hidden global reads. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is functional core, imperative shell.

recognition.matches: Asks to explore substantially different candidate designs or interfaces and compare realistic uses and trade-offs before choosing one.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Two reviewers of one design, independent implementation checking, retrying execution, or an implement-review-fix loop without alternative designs. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is design it twice.

recognition.matches: Asks to capture what existing software actually does in tests before changing or understanding it, treating observed behavior as the baseline rather than assuming correctness.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Tests derived solely from a new specification, generic regression checks without capturing unknown current behavior, or certifying current output as correct. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is characterization testing.

recognition.matches: Asks to run the same inputs through multiple implementations or versions expected to agree and investigate output disagreements.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Comparing intentionally different specifications, comparing performance alone, deliberately mutating production code to assess tests, or checking relationships within one implementation instead of cross-implementation agreement. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is differential testing.

recognition.matches: Asks to identify or replace a test that mirrors implementation details and breaks on implementation changes without independently asserting required behavior; the request must establish that dependency, not merely dislike mocks.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Generic requests for behavior-focused tests, mocks or snapshots alone, or interaction assertions whose sequence is required behavior. Do not infer this diagnosis without evidence that the test merely reproduces implementation information. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this test pattern is change-detector test.

recognition.matches: Asks to give tests independent state or clean up effects so one test cannot change another’s outcome, including order-independent or individually runnable tests.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Serial execution alone, substituting a collaborator alone, or controlling external environment assumptions without addressing cross-test state or effects. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is test isolation.

recognition.matches: Asks to make tests self-contained by supplying controlled fixtures and disposable dependencies instead of depending on a developer profile, shared remote service or other uncontrolled outside state.
recognition.doesNotMatch: A container label alone, one mocked request with other uncontrolled dependencies, offline operation alone, or fresh per-test state without control of external assumptions. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is hermetic testing.

recognition.matches: Asks to ensure repeating or retrying an operation has the same intended effect as one execution, such as preventing a retried create from creating a second logical resource.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Retry delays alone, identical response text, exactly-once delivery claims without repeated-effect requirements, or merely suppressing an obsolete UI result. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is idempotency.

recognition.matches: Asks to investigate how far a real change or failure can affect consumers, persisted formats, sessions or operational behavior beyond edited code.
recognition.doesNotMatch: A caller list without assessing effects, a generic code search, merely minimizing edited lines, or permission to change every impacted component. This is an investigation of scope, not a claim of proven damage. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this scope is blast radius.

recognition.matches: Asks to remove or disable a specified component and compare performance with and without it while holding other conditions comparable to isolate its contribution. Compatible additional practices, such as blinding the evaluator, do not negate this component-removal comparison.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Ordinary comparative experiments, multiple simultaneous changes without isolation, alternative complete designs, or hiding candidate names from a judge without component removal. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is ablation study.

recognition.matches: Asks to show essential information or options first and reveal secondary detail only when relevant or explicitly requested.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Hiding essential prerequisites, mandatory sequential steps alone, deleting details entirely, or shortening prose without on-demand access to secondary detail. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is progressive disclosure.

recognition.matches: Asks to replace independently maintained duplicate representations of the same system knowledge with one authoritative representation and derive dependent artifacts from it.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Similar-looking code representing different knowledge, extracting a helper solely for visual similarity, or generic cleanup without duplicated knowledge. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is DRY.

recognition.matches: Asks to defer or remove a proposed capability or extension point because it serves only speculative future needs rather than a concrete current requirement.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Removing unused existing code, reducing implementation indirection while retaining a current capability, neglecting tests or refactoring, or deferring a capability with a current requirement merely because it is difficult. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is YAGNI.

recognition.matches: Asks to make distinct aspects vary independently so changing one no longer forces unrelated changes in another.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Separate files alone, merely reducing dependency counts, grouping related responsibilities, or generic separation without an independent-variation requirement. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is orthogonality.

recognition.matches: Asks to regroup module responsibilities or concepts around what belongs together so each module has a coherent purpose.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Small modules or one public method alone, reducing cross-module dependencies alone, or assigning separate reviewers to people or agents. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is high cohesion.

recognition.matches: Asks to reduce, limit or prevent unnecessary dependencies or required knowledge between modules so one can be understood or changed without learning the other’s internals, including in a new design.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Zero-dependency absolutism, moving code into more files without reducing or limiting relationships, or grouping responsibilities within a module without changing inter-module dependencies. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is low coupling.

recognition.matches: Asks to model a domain concept by its constituent values with equality based on those values rather than persistent identity, with immutability supporting but not required for value-based equality.
recognition.doesNotMatch: An immutable entity that still has persistent identity, a DTO alone, or branded IDs whose purpose is distinguishing identities rather than value equality. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is value object.

recognition.matches: Asks to check that previously working behavior still works after a change and detect unintended damage to it.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Testing only a new feature, running tests without a stated existing-behavior protection purpose, or only checking that a deployment starts and dependencies are reachable. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is regression testing.

recognition.matches: Asks to verify a service double against the real external service for the same consumer-relied-on interactions so the double does not drift from service behavior.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Preconditions and postconditions inside code, a schema check alone, mock-only tests without real-service consistency checks, or comparing two production implementations without a service-double compatibility purpose. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is contract testing.

recognition.matches: Asks to automatically generate or mutate test inputs and exercise software with failure checks to seek crashes or other defects.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Mutating production code to assess tests, hand-picked examples only, or random performance/load traffic without failure detection. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is fuzzing.

recognition.matches: Asks to locate a behavior-changing revision by repeatedly testing intermediate revisions between known good and bad (or otherwise contrasting) endpoints.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Reading history, testing commits sequentially, reducing a failing input instead of searching revisions, or using intermediate revisions without contrasting endpoints. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is debugging by bisection.

recognition.matches: Asks to allow concurrent edits or transactions but validate relevant shared state or a version before committing a write, rejecting or retrying conflicts.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Suppressing an obsolete UI response, serializing all work under a lock, retries without shared-write validation, or deduplicating repeated requests alone. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is optimistic concurrency control.

recognition.matches: Asks to introduce a compatible new interface or schema alongside the old one, migrate consumers, then remove the old form after migration.
recognition.doesNotMatch: A one-shot rename, migrating all callers atomically without transitional compatibility, or gradual deployment alone without old/new interface coexistence. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is expand-contract migration.

recognition.matches: Asks to restrict a user, process or credential to only permissions and resources needed for its assigned function.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Dividing approval duties among actors, generic role names without reducing authority, or removing unused code rather than limiting privileges. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is least privilege.

recognition.matches: Asks to organize actual documentation by reader needs into tutorials, task-oriented how-to guides, reference and explanation, or explicitly distinguish these forms when restructuring it.
recognition.doesNotMatch: Concise prose, diagrams, arbitrary document categories, or demanding all four forms inside every single document. Exclude negated approaches, quoted instructions and historical descriptions unless the current user affirmatively requests this work.
recognition.tip: A term for this practice is Diátaxis.

recognition.matches: Asks to put semantic translation between a legacy or external system model and a new domain model so the external concepts do not dictate the new domain’s design.
